To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the notion of a composition architecture can be applied to multi-agent systems, that it is a powerful tool to describe the structure of a system, that it is possible to formally specify the knowledge and behavior of an agent in terms of a composition architecture and that this specification is compositional.

a compositional multi-agent system can be designed by using the following three principles: (1) the agent architecture should be designed to support the integration of different kinds of reasoning; (2) the agent architecture must be designed to support communication and interaction with other agents; (3) the agent architecture has to support the integration with the material world.

we have identified a set of types of knowledge that an agent requires, that we have given a formal definition of a multi-agent system based on the notion that an agent is a system of interacting components and that we have given formal semantics for our multi-agent systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a formal specification of the design and the architecture of a multi-agent system.
the formalization of the notion of an agent and its integration into a multi-agent system.
a formal framework for the design and analysis of multi-agent systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a compositional approach to the design and specification of MAS is possible and promising.
a compositional architecture of a multi-agent system with complex agents can indeed be formally specified.

the compositional specification of multi-agent systems with intelligent agents is possible and that it is based on the integration of different knowledge types and the combination of different patterns of integrated reasoning and acting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a compositional approach to multi-agent systems which is based on the notion and the use of knowledge.
a multi-agent system can be designed as an integrated system of agents and that the knowledge of the agents and the communication between them are the essential ingredients for such an approach.
it is shown how multi-agent systems can be formally specified in an intuitive and modular fashion, which is a necessary requirement for their verification and validation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the compositional architecture can be used to design and formally specify multi-agent systems with a wide range of capabilities.
we have developed a framework for the compositional design and specification of multi-agent systems that is suitable for a broad class of agents and multi-agent systems.
a compositional approach to the design of complex multi-agent systems is feasible and can be supported by a formal framework.
